key_insight: Intensity normalisation can modestly improve MRI segmentation generalisability, but it cannot fully overcome large cross-dataset domain shift.
clinical_relevance: For clinical deployment of knee MRI segmentation models, choosing a robust normalisation method may help external performance, yet broader domain-adaptation strategies are still needed.
method: Compared seven intensity normalisation methods: standard scaling, histogram-based techniques, CLAHE, and a GMM-based approach.
Trained a 3D U-Net for meniscus segmentation on the IWOAI 2019 dataset.
Evaluated performance on both internal and external test data (SKM-TEA) to test cross-domain generalisability.
evidence_signal: Internal performance was similar across methods, but external evaluation showed significant differences, with Z-score, Nyúl histogram matching, and CLAHE performing more robustly.
watch_item: The observed gains from normalisation were small relative to the substantial performance drop between datasets, so results may not generalise without additional domain-shift mitigation.
paper_title: A Systematic Benchmark of Intensity Normalisation Methods for 3D Knee MRI Segmentation and Cross-Domain Generalisability
